subject: MSA redline: allocation of IP defense and evidence delivery timeline
messages:
--- Message 1/4 ---
From: Jill Harper <jill.harper@acmecorp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Sullivan <msullivan@acmecorp.com>, ACME Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2025-05-21 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redline — initial questions on IP defense allocation

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We've attached our latest consolidated redline (Acme_MSA_redline_v3.docx) — the two open items from our side are: 1) a firm statement that ACME will be able to nominate counsel for third-party IP claims where the alleged infringement arises from ACME's use of the integration, and 2) a practical definition of what "evidence" we should expect to receive from Redwood to triage the claim within our SLA window.

Can you confirm Redwood's willingness to:
- Accept nomination in limited cases (our procurement prefers this for critical vendor plug-ins), or
- Alternatively, take lead defense but provide an evidence package within 48 hours of notice?

We'd also like to see an explicit evidence checklist and an ETA on when Redwood can deliver it.

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement is timeboxed this week.

Regards,
Jill Harper
Senior Procurement Manager
AcmeCorp

--- Message 3/4 ---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: legal-team@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-21 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redline — initial questions on IP defense allocation

Folks — my quick take for a reply we can send to ACME this afternoon:

Position (legal):
- Default: Redwood retains right to control defense for third-party IP claims that relate to our models/platform.
- Nomination: we can accept ACME nominating counsel only if the claim is solely about ACME modifications or customer-supplied data that introduces the risk; nomination subject to Redwood's prior written consent and standard privilege protections.

Evidence package (we can commit to):
- Written claim notice (complaint or takedown).
- Sample prompt and any supplied dataset excerpts that reasonably replicate the issue (redacted PII ok).
- Relevant model name & version, inference logs showing the request/response (token-level redaction allowed), and timestamped KV cache entries where available.
- System/config snapshot (runtime params, model quantization profile) and any integration code snippet limited to request path.

Delivery SLA: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide an initial evidence package within 48 hours of validated notice; complete forensic pack within 7 business days.

Redlines to propose (high level):
- Add a clause: Redwood shall have the first right to control defense for claims arising from its service; if ACME requests nomination, parties will meet within 24 hours to determine scope; nomination only with mutual agreement and subject to Redwood's right to approve counsel.
- Define evidence items (as above) as "reasonable requests" and tie SLAs to receipt of a valid legal notice.

Open questions for commercial:
- Are we comfortable with a 48-hour initial evidence SLA for all enterprise customers? If not, propose tiered SLAs for dedicated/private deployments.
- If we accept nomination in limited cases, what's the acceptable commercial offset? (credit, POI cap change, or insurance-first language)

I can draft suggested language and an evidence checklist doc (EvidenceChecklist.xlsx) — will attach when ready.

Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: EvidenceChecklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

--- Message 4/4 ---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-22 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redline — initial questions on IP defense allocation

Thanks Kim — agree with the legal framing. My commercial suggestion to close quickly:

- Accept Redwood control-by-default with a narrowly scoped nomination carve-out for customer-introduced modifications.
- Offer: if ACME insists on nomination in a covered case, Redwood will
  * agree to consider nominee but retain veto rights over counsel,
  * apply a one-time implementation credit of 5% of the first-year committed ARR (capped at $25k) as a compromise to their procurement team, and
  * require ACME maintain insurance primary for claims arising from their data/extensions.

That gives procurement a tangible concession while preserving our defense control and limiting financial exposure.

Next steps: Kim, can you send the redlined clause and the evidence checklist to Jill with the 48-hour initial pack SLA and the nomination constraints? I'll include the commercial concession language and loop in finance for the credit approval.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
